I am 63 and I never went to school. I have worked these 14 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My father taught me how to read the soil and the sky, and now I watch what my neighbors do. Some of my family work in the city and send money home, but this land is still my responsibility and I cannot afford a bad year.

Last year I put 10 mu into wheat and then maize, and 4 mu into cotton. The wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu, the maize about 600 kg, and the cotton about 260 kg. This year I will keep the same split because that is what my well, my labor, and my money allow.

For wheat, I always plough the land deep before sowing in October. I put one 40 kg bag of compound fertilizer on each mu as base, and then at green-up time in March I spread another 25 kg of urea per mu. I do not know the numbers written on the bag, but that is what I have always done and it works. My neighbor Lao Wang does the same and his wheat is always strong. I irrigate three times from the well: once when the wheat wakes up in spring, once when it shoots up tall, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice: herbicide first, then one more time for bugs and rust. I expect 500 kg per mu if the frost does not kill it early.

For maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in June, I plant the maize without ploughing again. I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer in the row at planting and then when the plants are knee-high I top-dress with 25 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate two times: one when it tassels, one when the grain fills. Two sprays: herbicide at the start, then something for the armyworms later. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton, I keep 4 mu because the price is okay and my wife can help pick it. I rotary-till that ground in April because cotton needs loose soil. I put one 40 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then I feed it twice more with urea: 15 kg each time, so 30 kg urea total per mu. Cotton stays longer and needs strength. It drinks more water, so I irrigate three times. It also gets more bugs than grain, so I spray four times. I hope for 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Money is tight. Every bag of fertilizer is real cash out of my pocket. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for medicine or repairs. Wasting some fertilizer just means I earn less. When I am unsure, I do what I did last year. If I see everyone in the village putting 25 kg of urea on wheat, I put 25 kg too. I do not trust new ideas unless I saw them work on Lao Wang's field first.
